audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers gave opposite answers on six of seven rows: full said Irelia/Irelia/Irelia/Irelia/Skill/Skill/Skill, content and packet said Skill/Skill/Skill/Annie/Annie/Irelia/Irelia.
audit.why: Levels 1-3 are genuinely close — Bladesurge pokes off minions but a 600-range dash lands her inside Annie's 625. Annie owns 4-6, and Irelia takes over on her first item.
audit.corrected: Full sides aligned to the content/packet chart; ratings adjusted to follow.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[3] credited the levels 4-5 swing to 'Tibbers' presence' — Tibbers does not exist until level 6.
audit.why: The real reason 4-5 belongs to Annie is Defiant Dance: it reduces physical damage during the charge, so Irelia's only damage-mitigation ability does nothing against Annie's magic burst.
audit.corrected: whys[3] and phases[3].why rebuilt around Defiant Dance's physical-only reduction.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two fabricated mechanics. (a) spikes[2] and late both say Ionian Fervor gives 'true damage' — it does not. (b) Both say her burst goes through 'your Tibbers shield'; Tibbers is a summoned pet, not a shield. Separately, Defiant Dance's physical-only reduction — the single most useful fact in this matchup for a mage — appeared nowhere.
audit.why: Riot text for Ionian Fervor: stacking bonus Attack Speed, and at maximum stacks bonus damage on hit. No true damage anywhere in the kit. Annie's E is her shield; her R is a pet.
audit.corrected: True damage replaced with attack speed plus on-hit; the shield language removed; Defiant Dance written into breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[1].d, phases[3].why and whys[3].

audit.whatIsWrong: Neither of the two flagged interactions reached the page: Bladesurge's healing, and Vanguard's Edge forming a wall behind you.
audit.why: Riot text: Bladesurge heals Irelia and refreshes on a Marked target or a kill, so extended trades pay her back — Grievous Wounds timing decides them. Vanguard's Edge's blades form a wall that damages and slows anyone walking through, and Annie has no dash, so Flash is reserved for the wall rather than the damage.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal written into breakdown.feeding and dontsFull[0].d; the wall into phases[6].why, spikes[3], late and wants.foe[3].

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[2].d called a wasted Flawless Duet a 'fifteen-second invitation'.
audit.corrected: Sixteen seconds stated, and the 850-range converging-blades shape given so the dodge is actionable.

notes: Two fabricated mechanics removed: Ionian Fervor does not grant true damage (attack speed, plus bonus on-hit at max stacks), and Tibbers is a pet, not a shield — both claims appeared twice. Tenacity claims were also stripped rather than restated: the kit file cannot establish tenacity behaviour, so spikes[3], whys[6] and wants.foe[3] were re-grounded on Vanguard's Edge's wall, which Riot's text does describe. Highest-value addition for an Annie player: Defiant Dance reduces PHYSICAL damage only, so her one mitigation ability is inert against every spell Annie casts — that was absent from the page entirely. Derived-flag note: Flawless Duet carries a 'grounding' flag that Riot's description does not support (damaged, stunned and Marked only); no grounding claim was written.
